quote: That it was gonna cost me a $127 a month. And I was like, that's no savings.
stewart_read: The customer hands over both a competing quote ($127/mo) and his own bill amount unprompted — a full bill-anchor setup already assembled for the rep. This is a gift moment the rep needs to seize with a flip, not just log.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to recognize when the customer volunteers both numbers at once — this is the cue to move straight into the objection_inversion flip, not a verify-question moment.

quote: Yeah. I mean, isn't isn't that less than what your average bill is?
stewart_read: This is the rep's only attempt at reframing the cost gap, but it's posed as a tentative question rather than a confident flip ('what's actually expensive is staying on Dominion's bill'). The customer immediately dismisses it and the rep does not press further.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive read: rep genuinely didn't have a stronger rebuttal queued and defaulted to restating the math. Strategic read (rejected): there's no evidence the soft phrasing was a deliberate pacing choice — the rep drops the thread entirely at 01:10 instead of building on it, which supports reactive over strategic.
coaching_implication: Replay this clip — show the rep how a declarative flip ('so you'd be paying $11 less and eventually paying nothing at all') lands harder than a hedged question.

quote: did you know that I don't know if you are aware, but solar actually has an end date. So once your panels are paid off, then you're you don't have an electric or a solar payment at all
stewart_read: Rather than creating curiosity about the customer's own numbers, the rep explains a general product feature (panels get paid off) — schema anti-pattern of selling features instead of anchoring to the customer's specific math.
coaching_implication: Redirect the rep to ask a curiosity question here instead — e.g. asking what the customer's bill would look like at year 10 or 15 — rather than a generic education statement.

quote: Hey. The lie was that the the Virginia Power was putting them up there for free, which I know is not true.
stewart_read: Customer raises a serious claim — that a rep or program told him panels would be free from the utility — but the rep's own team's involvement is unclear from context; the customer later clarifies it traces to a program on a website ('Dominion is supposed to be doing it... the program I looked at on the website'), which suggests this may be a third-party utility program confusion rather than an Ion or setter misrepresentation.
alternative_hypothesis: Alternative: this could be a prior Ion rep's overstatement that needs escalation. The customer's 01:46 clarification softens this toward third-party confusion, but the rep never explicitly confirms which company made the claim, so it remains unresolved either way.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to ask one clarifying question here — 'who told you that, was that one of our reps or something else you saw?' — to close the ambiguity live on the call rather than let it pass unaddressed.

quote: But I'm just gonna say, you could just cross me off, please.
stewart_read: Customer's final ask is a clean, calm opt-out after laying out a fully reasoned case; the rep accepts it immediately with no rebuttal attempt at all, closing the call in 8 seconds flat.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic read (rejected): there's no textbook rebuttal for 'remove me' once a customer has this fully reasoned a case, so a single soft acceptance may be appropriate rather than pushing into an unwinnable argument. But the schema calls for 3+ angles on cost objections before conceding, and the rep tried at most one soft angle (01:02), so this favors the reactive read.
coaching_implication: Use this as the anchor clip for multi_angle_resilience — show the rep how many angles were actually available (bill-flip, end-date framing repeated with numbers, clarifying the free-panels confusion) before conceding.

quote: Yeah. I talked to somebody, and I wasn't happy about what they told me. So I decided no. Thanks.
stewart_read: This opens as a callback to a prior conversation, but there is no evidence the rep has context on who the customer spoke with, what was pitched, or any handoff notes — the rep is diagnosing from scratch in real time.
coaching_implication: Flag to the manager as a process gap: if this is a recycled/repeat-touch lead, the rep should walk in with the prior quote details already known rather than reconstructing them live from the customer's frustrated recap.
